data.narrative:
Copenhagen Atomics is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised $25M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 3 private peers at same or adjacent stage (Valar Atomics at $6.0B in Series B, Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M in Seed, Fuse Energy at $200M in Series A) and 3 public nuclear equities, supplemented by a broader set of 8 private frontier nuclear players including Helion, X-Energy, and Oklo.

Two methods were applied. Stage-Progression applied a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $25M total raised proxy, implying a $50M valuation. Peer-Median analysis across the three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yielded a median valuation of $808M, with a range from $200M (Fuse Energy) to $6.0B (Valar Atomics). The wide dispersion reflects stage heterogeneity within the nuclear energy segment—Series B commands substantial premiums over Seed and Series A.

Triangulating these two methods produces a range of $42M to $929M, with a median of $429M. The stage-progression floor ($50M) reflects minimal step-up from current capital raised; the peer median ($808M) anchors the upper bound. Key uncertainties include: the degree to which later-stage peer valuations (Valar at Series B) should inform early-stage pricing, technology differentiation relative to the peer set, and path-to-commercialization risk in the nuclear sector.
